Every request to OpenWeatherMap Weather API 2.5 and Geocoding API 1.0 authenticates with an API key passed in the appid URL query parameter over HTTPS. For account registration, key generation, and environment variable setup, see Get your API key.

Attribute Specification Parameter appid Location Query string Type and format string—32-character lowercase hexadecimal token (such as a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90) HTTP header authentication Unsupported—Authorization and X-API-Key headers are rejected and trigger CORS preflight failures in browsers Transport security HTTPS required to encrypt the query string in transit Key activation window 10–15 minutes typical; up to 2 hours maximum Multiple keys Supported per account; all keys share the account rate-limit quota

Append appid as a query parameter on every HTTPS request: GET https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?lat=51.5085&lon=-0.1257&appid={API_KEY} Parameter Type Required Default Description appid string Yes — 32-character lowercase hexadecimal API key associated with your OpenWeatherMap account. Credential exposure in client applications Because appid travels in the URL query string, calling api.openweathermap.org directly from browser JavaScript or mobile clients exposes your key in browser developer tools and network logs. Route client requests through a backend proxy as shown in Set up rate limiting and caching.

When authentication fails, the API responds with HTTP 401 Unauthorized and a JSON payload containing a numeric cod field: { "cod": 401, "message": "Invalid API key. See https://openweathermap.org/faq#error401 for more info." }

OpenWeatherMap returns 401 Unauthorized under four conditions: Trigger Condition Missing appid The request URL omits the appid query parameter, passes an empty value (appid=), or supplies the key in an HTTP header instead of the query string. Invalid or revoked key The appid value contains a typo, extra whitespace, or belongs to a key that was deleted or deactivated on the OpenWeatherMap dashboard. Newly generated key pending activation The key was created within the past 2 hours and has not finished propagating across OpenWeatherMap edge servers (10–15 minutes typical; up to 2 hours maximum). Endpoint outside subscription plan The key is valid and active, but the request targets an endpoint outside your active subscription tier, such as One Call API 3.0 (/data/3.0/onecall) or 16-day daily forecast (/data/2.5/forecast/daily) without an active plan for that product. For additional status codes and error schemas, see Error codes. For account quota rules across keys, see Rate limits.
Returns current weather observations for a geographic coordinate pair (lat and lon). For implementation workflows, see Use geographic coordinates and Get current weather by city.
GET https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather

Parameter Type Required Default Description lat number Yes — Latitude in decimal degrees, ranging from -90 to 90 (positive for north, negative for south). lon number Yes — Longitude in decimal degrees, ranging from -180 to 180 (positive for east, negative for west). appid string Yes — 32-character hexadecimal API key. See Authentication. units string No standard Measurement system for temperature and wind speed: standard (Kelvin, m/s), metric (Celsius, m/s), or imperial (Fahrenheit, mph). See Unit systems and conversions. lang string No en Language code for the localized weather[].description value (such as es, fr, de, ja, or pt_br). mode string No json Response payload format: json, xml, or html.

Built-in geocoding deprecation OpenWeatherMap deprecated built-in city-name, city-ID, and postal-code lookups on weather endpoints. Although q, id, and zip remain functional for backward compatibility, resolve place names and postal codes to coordinates first through the Geocoding endpoints and pass lat and lon to this endpoint. Supply one legacy identifier only when omitting lat and lon: Parameter Type Required Default Description q string Conditional — Deprecated. Comma-separated city name, state code (US locations only), and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code formatted as {city},{state},{country} (for example, London,GB or Portland,OR,US). URL-encode spaces and special characters. id number Conditional — Deprecated. OpenWeatherMap numeric city identifier (for example, 2643743 for London). zip string Conditional — Deprecated. Postal or ZIP code and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code formatted as {zip},{country} (for example, 94040,US or EC1A,GB). Defaults to US when the country code is omitted.

curl Node.js Python curl --get "https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather" \ --data-urlencode "lat=51.5085" \ --data-urlencode "lon=-0.1257" \ --data-urlencode "units=metric" \ --data-urlencode "appid=$OPENWEATHER_API_KEY" const params = new URLSearchParams({ lat: '51.5085', lon: '-0.1257', units: 'metric', appid: process.env.OPENWEATHER_API_KEY, }); const response = await fetch( `https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?${params}`, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10000) } ); if (!response.ok) { throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`); } const data = await response.json(); console.log(data); import os import requests response = requests.get( "https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather", params={ "lat": 51.5085, "lon": -0.1257, "units": "metric", "appid": os.environ["OPENWEATHER_API_KEY"], }, timeout=10, ) response.raise_for_status() data = response.json() print(data)
curl --get "https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather" \ --data-urlencode "q=London,GB" \ --data-urlencode "units=metric" \ --data-urlencode "appid=$OPENWEATHER_API_KEY"

Example 200 OK JSON payload requested with units=metric: { "coord": { "lon": -0.1257, "lat": 51.5085 }, "weather": [ { "id": 500, "main": "Rain", "description": "light rain", "icon": "10d" } ], "base": "stations", "main": { "temp": 12.3, "feels_like": 11.7, "temp_min": 10.8, "temp_max": 13.4, "pressure": 1015, "sea_level": 1015, "grnd_level": 1011, "humidity": 84 }, "visibility": 10000, "wind": { "speed": 5.2, "deg": 230, "gust": 8.1 }, "rain": { "1h": 0.65 }, "clouds": { "all": 90 }, "dt": 1715270400, "sys": { "type": 2, "id": 2075535, "country": "GB", "sunrise": 1715230800, "sunset": 1715284800 }, "timezone": 3600, "id": 2643743, "name": "London", "cod": 200 }

Field Type Unit Description coord.lon number Decimal degrees Longitude of the matched location (-180 to 180). coord.lat number Decimal degrees Latitude of the matched location (-90 to 90). weather array — List of weather condition objects. The first element (weather[0]) represents the primary condition. weather[].id number — Numeric weather condition code. See OpenWeatherMap weather condition codes. weather[].main string — Weather condition category: Thunderstorm, Drizzle, Rain, Snow, Atmosphere (serialized as specific 7xx phenomenon names such as Mist, Smoke, Haze, Dust, Fog, Sand, Ash, Squall, or Tornado), Clear, or Clouds. weather[].description string — Localized condition description within the category, controlled by lang. weather[].icon string — Icon identifier (such as 10d for day or 10n for night). See OpenWeatherMap weather condition codes. base string — Internal OpenWeatherMap parameter indicating the observation source (such as stations). main.temp number K, °C, or °F Current air temperature (Kelvin for standard, Celsius for metric, Fahrenheit for imperial). main.feels_like number K, °C, or °F Human-perceived temperature accounting for wind chill and relative humidity. main.temp_min number K, °C, or °F Lowest currently observed temperature across stations within a large metropolitan or extended area. Represents instantaneous spatial spread rather than a 24-hour daily low. main.temp_max number K, °C, or °F Highest currently observed temperature across stations within a large metropolitan or extended area. Represents instantaneous spatial spread rather than a 24-hour daily high. main.pressure number hPa Atmospheric pressure at sea level (when sea_level and grnd_level are absent) or station reference pressure. main.sea_level number hPa Optional. Atmospheric pressure adjusted to mean sea level. main.grnd_level number hPa Optional. Atmospheric pressure measured at local ground elevation. main.humidity number % Relative humidity percentage (0–100). visibility number m Horizontal visibility distance in meters, capped at a maximum of 10000 (10 km). wind.speed number m/s or mph Sustained wind speed (m/s for standard and metric; mph for imperial). wind.deg number Degrees Meteorological wind direction (0–360, indicating the direction from which wind blows). wind.gust number m/s or mph Optional. Peak wind gust speed (m/s for standard and metric; mph for imperial). Omitted when unavailable. clouds.all number % Cloudiness percentage (0–100). rain.1h number mm Optional. Liquid precipitation volume for the past 1 hour. Omitted when no rain occurred. snow.1h number mm Optional. Snow liquid-equivalent precipitation volume for the past 1 hour. Omitted when no snow occurred. dt number Unix UTC (s) Observation calculation timestamp in Unix epoch seconds (UTC). sys.type number — Optional. Internal OpenWeatherMap system parameter. sys.id number — Optional. Internal OpenWeatherMap station identifier. sys.country string — ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (for example, GB or US). sys.sunrise number Unix UTC (s) Sunrise time in Unix epoch seconds (UTC). sys.sunset number Unix UTC (s) Sunset time in Unix epoch seconds (UTC). timezone number s Offset in seconds from UTC for the local time zone (for example, 3600 for UTC+1). id number — Deprecated OpenWeatherMap city identifier. name string — Deprecated matched locality name (returns an empty string for unpopulated or open-ocean coordinates). cod number — Internal status code (200 as a JSON number on success).

Status code Meaning Description 200 OK Current weather payload returned (cod is 200). 400 Bad Request Missing location parameters or out-of-range coordinates (cod is "400"). 401 Unauthorized Missing, invalid, inactive, or unauthorized appid (cod is 401). 404 Not Found Legacy q, id, or zip lookup matched no record (cod is "404"). 429 Too Many Requests Account rate limit exceeded (cod is 429). 5xx Server Error Upstream OpenWeatherMap server or gateway error. For full error payload schemas and cod type behavior, see Error codes.

OpenWeatherMap Weather API 2.5 and Geocoding API 1.0 report request outcomes through HTTP status codes paired with a JSON response body. For retry policies, timeout guards, and safe JSON parsing patterns, see Handle errors in production and Common errors.

Status code Meaning Description 200 OK Request succeeded. Returns a JSON object or JSON array depending on the endpoint. 400 Bad Request Request is missing a required parameter or contains an invalid parameter value, such as omitted coordinates ("Nothing to geocode") or out-of-range latitude and longitude ("wrong latitude" or "wrong longitude"). 401 Unauthorized Authentication failed due to a missing appid, an invalid or revoked key, a newly generated key awaiting activation, or an endpoint outside your subscription plan. See Authentication. 404 Not Found Requested city name, city ID, postal code, or endpoint path does not exist. Whereas /geo/1.0/zip returns 404 for unknown postal codes, /geo/1.0/direct and /geo/1.0/reverse return 200 OK with an empty array ([]). 429 Too Many Requests Request exceeded the account rate limit (60 calls per minute on the free tier) or monthly quota. See Rate limits. 500 Internal Server Error Unhandled server error on OpenWeatherMap application nodes. 502 / 503 / 504 Bad Gateway / Service Unavailable / Gateway Timeout Transient upstream load balancer or reverse proxy failure. Responses can return an HTML document (text/html) rather than a JSON payload.

Application-layer 4xx and 500 errors return a JSON object with the following fields: Field Type Description cod number | string Internal status code mirroring the HTTP status code. Serialized as either a number or a string depending on the status code and endpoint. message string Human-readable diagnostic description of the error condition.

OpenWeatherMap serializes the cod property inconsistently across endpoints and status codes. Inspect the HTTP transport status code (response.status in Node.js or response.status_code in Python) instead of comparing cod with strict type equality. HTTP status /data/2.5/weather /data/2.5/forecast /geo/1.0/direct and /geo/1.0/reverse /geo/1.0/zip 200 OK number (200) string ("200") Absent (root is JSON array []) Absent (root is location object) 400 Bad Request string ("400") string ("400") string ("400") string ("400") 401 Unauthorized number (401) number (401) number (401) number (401) 404 Not Found string ("404") string ("404") Not returned for unmatched queries (200 with []) string ("404") 429 Too Many Requests number (429) number (429) number (429) number (429) 500 Internal Server Error number or string number or string number or string number or string 502 / 503 / 504 Absent if HTML gateway body Absent if HTML gateway body Absent if HTML gateway body Absent if HTML gateway body
Returned when required location parameters are missing or empty, or when lat or lon falls outside valid geographic bounds: { "cod": "400", "message": "Nothing to geocode" }

Returned when appid is missing, invalid, pending activation, or unauthorized for the target endpoint: { "cod": 401, "message": "Invalid API key. See https://openweathermap.org/faq#error401 for more info." }
Returned when a city query on /data/2.5/weather or /data/2.5/forecast or a postal code on /geo/1.0/zip matches no record: { "cod": "404", "message": "city not found" }

Returned when account request volume exceeds your subscription rate limit: { "cod": 429, "message": "Your account is temporary blocked due to exceeding of requests limitation of your subscription type." }

Returns 3-hour weather forecast intervals across 5 days (up to 40 intervals) for a geographic coordinate pair (lat and lon). For daily aggregation and precipitation filtering patterns, see Get a 5-day forecast.
GET https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/forecast

Parameter Type Required Default Description lat number Yes — Latitude in decimal degrees, ranging from -90 to 90 (positive for north, negative for south). lon number Yes — Longitude in decimal degrees, ranging from -180 to 180 (positive for east, negative for west). appid string Yes — 32-character hexadecimal API key. See Authentication. units string No standard Measurement system for temperature and wind speed: standard (Kelvin, m/s), metric (Celsius, m/s), or imperial (Fahrenheit, mph). See Unit systems and conversions. cnt number No 40 Number of chronological 3-hour forecast intervals to return, from 1 to 40 across 5 days (for example, 8 covers 24 hours). lang string No en Language code for the localized list[].weather[].description value (such as es, fr, de, ja, or pt_br). mode string No json Response payload format: json or xml.

Although q, id, and zip remain functional for backward compatibility, resolve place names and postal codes to coordinates first through the Geocoding endpoints and pass lat and lon to this endpoint. Supply one legacy identifier only when omitting lat and lon: Parameter Type Required Default Description q string Conditional — Deprecated. Comma-separated city name, state code (US locations only), and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code formatted as {city},{state},{country} (for example, London,GB or Portland,OR,US). Example 200 OK JSON payload requested with units=metric and cnt=2 (showing one daytime rainy interval and one nighttime cloudy interval alongside the city object): { "cod": "200", "message": 0, "cnt": 2, "list": [ { "dt": 1715277600, "main": { "temp": 14.2, "feels_like": 13.6, "temp_min": 13.8, "temp_max": 14.2, "pressure": 1015, "sea_level": 1015, "grnd_level": 1011, "humidity": 76, "temp_kf": 0.4 }, "weather": [ { "id": 500, "main": "Rain", "description": "light rain", "icon": "10d" } ], "clouds": { "all": 88 }, "wind": { "speed": 4.6, "deg": 225, "gust": 7.4 }, "visibility": 10000, "pop": 0.64, "rain": { "3h": 0.82 }, "sys": { "pod": "d" }, "dt_txt": "2024-05-09 18:00:00" }, { "dt": 1715288400, "main": { "temp": 11.1, "feels_like": 10.4, "temp_min": 11.1, "temp_max": 11.1, "pressure": 1017, "sea_level": 1017, "grnd_level": 1013, "humidity": 82, "temp_kf": 0 }, "weather": [ { "id": 803, "main": "Clouds", "description": "broken clouds", "icon": "04n" } ], "clouds": { "all": 62 }, "wind": { "speed": 3.1, "deg": 240, "gust": 5.2 }, "visibility": 10000, "pop": 0.12, "sys": { "pod": "n" }, "dt_txt": "2024-05-09 21:00:00" } ], "city": { "id": 2643743, "name": "London", "coord": { "lat": 51.5085, "lon": -0.1257 }, "country": "GB", "population": 1000000, "timezone": 3600, "sunrise": 1715230800, "sunset": 1715284800 } }

Field Type Unit Description cod string — Internal status code. Returned as the string "200" on success, unlike the integer 200 returned by the Current weather endpoint. message number — Internal OpenWeatherMap response parameter (0 on normal responses). cnt number — Number of 3-hour forecast intervals returned in list (1–40). list array — Chronologically ordered array of 3-hour forecast interval objects. list[].dt number Unix UTC (s) Forecasted interval timestamp in Unix epoch seconds (UTC). list[].main.temp number K, °C, or °F Forecasted air temperature (Kelvin for standard, Celsius for metric, Fahrenheit for imperial). list[].main.feels_like number K, °C, or °F Human-perceived forecasted temperature accounting for wind chill and relative humidity. list[].main.temp_min number K, °C, or °F Optional internal minimum temperature bound at forecast calculation time. list[].main.temp_max number K, °C, or °F Optional internal maximum temperature bound at forecast calculation time. list[].main.pressure number hPa Forecasted atmospheric pressure at sea level by default. list[].main.sea_level number hPa Forecasted atmospheric pressure adjusted to mean sea level. list[].main.grnd_level number hPa Forecasted atmospheric pressure at local ground elevation. list[].main.humidity number % Forecasted relative humidity percentage (0–100). list[].main.temp_kf number K, °C, or °F Internal model calibration parameter. list[].weather array — List of weather condition objects for the interval (list[].weather[0] is primary). list[].weather[].id number — Numeric weather condition code. See OpenWeatherMap weather condition codes. list[].weather[].main string — Weather condition category (Thunderstorm, Drizzle, Rain, Snow, Atmosphere, Clear, or Clouds). list[].weather[].description string — Localized condition description within the category, controlled by lang. list[].weather[].icon string — Icon identifier (such as 10d or 04n). See OpenWeatherMap weather condition codes. list[].clouds.all number % Forecasted cloudiness percentage (0–100). list[].wind.speed number m/s or mph Forecasted sustained wind speed (m/s for standard and metric; mph for imperial). list[].wind.deg number Degrees Forecasted meteorological wind direction (0–360). list[].wind.gust number m/s or mph Optional. Forecasted peak wind gust speed (m/s for standard and metric; mph for imperial). list[].visibility number m Forecasted horizontal visibility in meters, capped at a maximum of 10000 (10 km). list[].pop number Ratio Probability of precipitation from 0.0 to 1.0 (0.0 equals 0%, 1.0 equals 100%). list[].rain.3h number mm Optional. Forecasted liquid precipitation volume over the preceding 3 hours. Omitted when no rain is forecasted. list[].snow.3h number mm Optional. Forecasted snow liquid-equivalent volume over the preceding 3 hours. Omitted when no snow is forecasted. list[].sys.pod string — Part of the day at the forecasted timestamp: "d" for day or "n" for night. list[].dt_txt string UTC Forecasted timestamp formatted as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS in UTC. city.id number — Deprecated OpenWeatherMap city identifier. city.name string — Matched locality name. city.coord.lat number Decimal degrees Latitude of the matched location (-90 to 90). city.coord.lon number Decimal degrees Longitude of the matched location (-180 to 180). city.country string — ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (for example, GB or US). city.population number — Estimated resident population of the matched locality. city.timezone number s Offset in seconds from UTC for the local time zone. city.sunrise number Unix UTC (s) Sunrise time in Unix epoch seconds (UTC). city.sunset number Unix UTC (s) Sunset time in Unix epoch seconds (UTC).

Status code Meaning Description 200 OK Forecast payload returned (cod is "200"). 400 Bad Request Missing location parameters, invalid cnt, or out-of-range coordinates (cod is "400"). 401 Unauthorized Missing, invalid, inactive, or unauthorized appid (cod is 401). 404 Not Found Legacy q, id, or zip lookup matched no record (cod is "404"). 429 Too Many Requests Account rate limit exceeded (cod is 429). 5xx Server Error Upstream OpenWeatherMap server or gateway error. For full error payload schemas and cod type behavior, see Error codes.

OpenWeatherMap Geocoding API 1.0 converts city names and postal codes into geographic coordinates (lat and lon) and converts coordinate pairs back into named localities. For two-step coordinate resolution and caching recipes, see Use geographic coordinates. Empty result behavior The /geo/1.0/direct and /geo/1.0/reverse endpoints return HTTP 200 OK with an empty JSON array ([]) when no location matches your query, rather than HTTP 404 Not Found. Always verify that the array contains at least one element before reading index 0. By contrast, /geo/1.0/zip returns HTTP 404 Not Found with a JSON error object when a postal code is unrecognized.
Resolves a city or locality name into up to 5 candidate coordinate records. GET https://api.openweathermap.org/geo/1.0/direct

Parameter Type Required Default Description q string Yes — Comma-separated city name, state code (US locations only), and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code formatted as {city},{state},{country} (for example, London,GB or Portland,OR,US). URL-encode spaces and special characters. limit number No 1 Maximum number of matching locations returned in the response array, from 1 to 5. appid string Yes — 32-character hexadecimal API key. See Authentication.

curl Node.js Python curl --get "https://api.openweathermap.org/geo/1.0/direct" \ --data-urlencode "q=London" \ --data-urlencode "limit=2" \ --data-urlencode "appid=$OPENWEATHER_API_KEY" const params = new URLSearchParams({ q: 'London', limit: '2', appid: process.env.OPENWEATHER_API_KEY, }); const response = await fetch( `https://api.openweathermap.org/geo/1.0/direct?${params}`, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10000) } ); if (!response.ok) { throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`); } const locations = await response.json(); console.log(locations); import os import requests response = requests.get( "https://api.openweathermap.org/geo/1.0/direct", params={ "q": "London", "limit": 2, "appid": os.environ["OPENWEATHER_API_KEY"], }, timeout=10, ) response.raise_for_status() locations = response.json() print(locations)

Example 200 OK JSON array payload (local_names abbreviated for readability): [ { "name": "London", "local_names": { "ascii": "London", "en": "London", "es": "Londres", "feature_name": "London", "fr": "Londres" }, "lat": 51.5073219, "lon": -0.1276474, "country": "GB", "state": "England" }, { "name": "London", "local_names": { "en": "London", "fr": "London" }, "lat": 42.9832406, "lon": -81.243372, "country": "CA", "state": "Ontario" } ]

The root response is a JSON array (0–5 elements). Each element contains the following fields: Field Type Unit Description name string — Canonical name of the matched locality. local_names object — Optional. Map of localized names and transliterations for the locality. local_names.<lang> string — Optional. Locality name translated into ISO language code <lang> (such as en, es, or fr). local_names.ascii string — Optional. ASCII transliteration of the locality name. local_names.feature_name string — Optional. Internal OpenWeatherMap geographic feature name. lat number Decimal degrees Latitude of the matched locality (-90 to 90). lon number Decimal degrees Longitude of the matched locality (-180 to 180). country string — ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (for example, GB or CA). state string — Optional. State, province, or administrative region name when available.
Resolves a postal or ZIP code and country code into a single geographic coordinate object. GET https://api.openweathermap.org/geo/1.0/zip
documents.s: Direct geocoding by postal or ZIP code

documents.t: Parameter Type Required Default Description zip string Yes — Postal or ZIP code and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code formatted as {zip code},{country code} (for example, E14,GB or 94040,US). Defaults to US when the country code is omitted. appid string Yes — 32-character hexadecimal API key. See Authentication.
curl --get "https://api.openweathermap.org/geo/1.0/zip" \ --data-urlencode "zip=E14,GB" \ --data-urlencode "appid=$OPENWEATHER_API_KEY"

Field Type Unit Description zip string — Matched postal or ZIP code. name string — Locality or district name associated with the postal code. lat number Decimal degrees Latitude of the postal area centroid (-90 to 90). lon number Decimal degrees Longitude of the postal area centroid (-180 to 180). country string — ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (for example, GB or US).
Resolves a geographic coordinate pair (lat and lon) into up to 5 nearby named localities. GET https://api.openweathermap.org/geo/1.0/reverse

Parameter Type Required Default Description lat number Yes — Latitude in decimal degrees, ranging from -90 to 90 (positive for north, negative for south). lon number Yes — Longitude in decimal degrees, ranging from -180 to 180 (positive for east, negative for west). limit number No 1 Maximum number of nearby localities returned in the response array, from 1 to 5. appid string Yes — 32-character hexadecimal API key. See Authentication.

curl --get "https://api.openweathermap.org/geo/1.0/reverse" \ --data-urlencode "lat=51.5098" \ --data-urlencode "lon=-0.1180" \ --data-urlencode "limit=1" \ --data-urlencode "appid=$OPENWEATHER_API_KEY"

Example 200 OK JSON array payload: [ { "name": "City of Westminster", "local_names": { "ascii": "City of Westminster", "en": "City of Westminster", "feature_name": "City of Westminster", "fr": "Cité de Westminster" }, "lat": 51.4973206, "lon": -0.137149, "country": "GB", "state": "England" } ]
Returns a JSON array (0–5 elements) using the identical element schema documented under Direct geocoding by place name (name, local_names, lat, lon, country, and state).

Status code Meaning Description 200 OK Request succeeded. Returns a JSON array on /direct and /reverse (including [] when no location matches) or a JSON object on /zip. 400 Bad Request Missing required query parameter ("Nothing to geocode") or out-of-range coordinates (cod is "400"). 401 Unauthorized Missing, invalid, inactive, or unauthorized appid (cod is 401). 404 Not Found Postal code not found on /geo/1.0/zip (cod is "404"). 429 Too Many Requests Account rate limit exceeded (cod is 429). 5xx Server Error Upstream OpenWeatherMap server or gateway error. For full error payload schemas and cod type behavior, see Error codes.

OpenWeatherMap enforces per-minute burst limits and monthly call quotas at the account level based on your subscription tier. For caching proxy architecture, client-side throttling, and backoff implementation patterns, see Set up rate limiting and caching.

Quota or attribute Free tier specification Calls per minute 60 calls/minute Calls per month 1,000,000 calls/month Included endpoints Current weather (/data/2.5/weather), 5-day forecast (/data/2.5/forecast), Geocoding (/geo/1.0/direct, /geo/1.0/zip, /geo/1.0/reverse), and Air pollution (/data/2.5/air_pollution) Model update interval Every 10 minutes Payment card required No

Pooled across all API keys: Creating multiple API keys under the same OpenWeatherMap account does not multiply your quota. Every active key on an account draws from a single shared pool of 60 calls per minute and 1,000,000 calls per month. Pooled across all free endpoints: Requests to Current weather, 5-day forecast, Geocoding, and Air pollution endpoints all increment the same account-level call counter. Two-step geocoding and weather lookups: Resolving a place name through /geo/1.0/direct and fetching observations through /data/2.5/weather without caching consumes 2 calls. Cache resolved coordinates persistently and cache weather payloads for up to the 10-minute model update interval. Free Weather API 2.5 vs. One Call API 3.0: Free Weather API 2.5 (/data/2.5/*) and Geocoding API 1.0 (/geo/1.0/*) require no credit card and include 1,000,000 calls per month with hard rate-limit blocking above quota. One Call API 3.0 (/data/3.0/onecall) is a separate "Pay as you call" subscription that requires a payment card, includes 1,000 free calls per day, and bills per overage increment unless you set a daily limit equal to 1,000 calls in your billing dashboard.

OpenWeatherMap Weather API 2.5 and Geocoding API 1.0 omit rate-limit telemetry headers—such as X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, and Retry-After—from both 200 OK and 429 Too Many Requests responses. Client applications must meter outbound request rates locally rather than reading remaining quota from HTTP response headers.

When combined traffic across your account's API keys exceeds 60 calls per minute or exhausts your monthly quota, the API returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with a numeric cod value (429) and temporarily blocks subsequent requests during a short cooldown window: { "cod": 429, "message": "Your account is temporary blocked due to exceeding of requests limitation of your subscription type." } For retry and exponential backoff handling on 429 responses, see Handle errors in production.
Use the diagnostic flow below to match what your HTTP client or browser console reports to the underlying root cause and recovery pattern.

The API rejects the query string before running a lookup and returns HTTP 400 with "cod": "400" (formatted as a string): { "cod": "400", "message": "Nothing to geocode" } Invalid geographic coordinates produce a coordinate-specific message: { "cod": "400", "message": "wrong latitude" }

Root cause Resolution Empty search input (?q=&appid=...) submitted before user typing completes Trim and validate that q or zip is non-empty before dispatching the request. Uninitialized JavaScript variables serialized as literals (?lat=undefined&lon=NaN) Guard numeric coordinates with Number.isFinite(lat) && Number.isFinite(lon) prior to calling fetch. Swapped GeoJSON coordinate order ([lon, lat] passed as lat and lon) Confirm lat lies within -90 to 90 and lon lies within -180 to 180. Unencoded # or & characters inside location text truncating the URL Construct URLs with URLSearchParams in JavaScript or params={...} in Python rather than string concatenation.

Log the serialized request URL with appid redacted and verify that either q or both lat and lon contain well-formed values: curl -i "https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?lat=51.5074&lon=-0.1278&units=metric&appid=$OPENWEATHER_API_KEY"
OpenWeatherMap rejects authentication and returns HTTP 401 with an integer cod value: { "cod": 401, "message": "Invalid API key." }

Root cause Resolution Newly created API key is still propagating across edge gateways Wait 10–15 minutes (and up to 2 hours in peak propagation windows) after creating a key before retesting. Do not delete and recreate the key while waiting, which resets the timer. Calling One Call API 3.0 (/data/3.0/onecall) or paid endpoints on a free key Free keys authorize /data/2.5/weather, /data/2.5/forecast, and /geo/1.0/* without billing setup. Calling /data/3.0/onecall, /data/2.5/forecast/daily, or historical endpoints without an active subscription returns 401 Unauthorized. Missing, misspelled, or whitespace-padded appid parameter Pass the credential as lowercase appid= (not api_key= or key=) and call .trim() on environment variables to strip trailing newline characters from .env files. Key was deactivated or deleted in your account Sign in to the OpenWeatherMap API keys dashboard and confirm the key status reads Active.

Isolate your API key from application code and .env loaders by testing a free-tier 2.5 endpoint directly from your terminal: curl -i "https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q=London,GB&appid=$OPENWEATHER_API_KEY" If this command returns HTTP/2 200 while your application receives 401, check whether your code targets /data/3.0/onecall or reads an empty environment variable. For credential setup details, see Authentication.

Missing locations surface differently depending on which OpenWeatherMap service you call: Weather API 2.5 (/data/2.5/weather and /data/2.5/forecast) returns HTTP 404 Not Found with "cod": "404" as a string: { "cod": "404", "message": "city not found" } Geocoding API 1.0 (/geo/1.0/direct) returns HTTP 200 OK with an empty JSON array when no location matches—causing unguarded data[0].lat reads to throw a runtime TypeError: []

Root cause Resolution Omitted service prefix (such as requesting /weather instead of /data/2.5/weather) Include the full versioned endpoint path (/data/2.5/weather, /data/2.5/forecast, or /geo/1.0/direct). Ambiguous, localized, or unencoded city name in ?q= URL-encode non-ASCII characters and spaces (São%20Paulo), or switch to the two-step Query weather by coordinates workflow. US state code supplied without ISO 3166 country code (?q=Austin,TX) Append ,US whenever specifying a US state (?q=Austin,TX,US). Non-US postal code passed to /geo/1.0/zip without a country code /geo/1.0/zip defaults to the United States when country is omitted; append the two-letter ISO country code (?zip=SW1A,GB). Unchecked empty array from /geo/1.0/direct Verify Array.isArray(results) && results.length > 0 before reading results[0].

Query the Geocoding API directly with limit=5 to inspect matching candidates and their canonical coordinates: curl -s "https://api.openweathermap.org/geo/1.0/direct?q=Springfield,IL,US&limit=5&appid=$OPENWEATHER_API_KEY"

Exceeding your subscription's burst or monthly quota returns HTTP 429: { "cod": 429, "message": "Your account is temporary blocked due to exceeding of requests limitation of your subscription type." }

Root cause Resolution Exceeding 60 calls per minute across all keys on your account Quotas pool across your entire OpenWeatherMap account rather than per individual key. Add a 10-minute backend cache instead of rotating extra keys. Runaway frontend useEffect or reactive state loop Open your browser DevTools Network tab to verify your component isn't re-fetching on every render; debounce search inputs by 300–500 ms. Unthrottled Promise.all or tight loop in scheduled batch jobs Space sequential batch requests by at least 1,100 ms (~54 requests/minute) and back off exponentially when 429 occurs. Direct client requests scaling linearly with concurrent website visitors Move OpenWeatherMap calls behind a shared caching proxy—see Set up rate limiting and caching.

When running background sync scripts across multiple saved cities, pace sequential calls so total throughput stays safely below 60 requests per minute: const PACE_INTERVAL_MS = 1100; const pause = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms)); for (let i = 0; i < locations.length; i += 1) { const weather = await fetchWeatherByCoordinates(locations[i].lat, locations[i].lon); results.push(weather); if (i < locations.length - 1) { await pause(PACE_INTERVAL_MS); } } For full exponential backoff and retry logic on 429 responses, see Handle errors in production.

No HTTP status code reaches your JavaScript fetch handler; instead, the browser console logs a Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) or mixed-content security error: Access to fetch at 'https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?...' from origin 'http://localhost:3000' has been blocked by CORS policy: Response to preflight request doesn't pass access control check. Or on an https:// site calling an http:// endpoint: Mixed Content: The page at 'https://example.com' was loaded over HTTPS, but requested an insecure resource 'http://api.openweathermap.org/...'. This request has been blocked.

Root cause Resolution Custom request headers (Authorization, Content-Type: application/json, X-Requested-With, or Cache-Control) attached by frontend HTTP interceptors Preflight-exempt GET requests carry no custom headers. Adding non-CORS-safelisted headers forces the browser to send an OPTIONS preflight check, which api.openweathermap.org rejects. Remove custom headers—or move the request to your backend. Hardcoded http://api.openweathermap.org URL called from an https:// page Always use https://api.openweathermap.org so browsers never block the request as mixed content. Calling OpenWeatherMap directly from production browser JavaScript Route frontend requests through your own backend proxy or serverless route (GET /api/weather), which eliminates browser CORS restrictions, hides appid from DevTools, and shares a 10-minute cache across users. See API architecture overview.

Inspect the Network tab in browser DevTools and look at the Method column: If you see a failed OPTIONS request preceding your GET request, inspect Request Headers to find which global Axios or Fetch interceptor injected Authorization or Content-Type. Verify the target URL starts with https://api.openweathermap.org and passes appid in the query string on your backend proxy.

When a request succeeds with 200 OK yet your UI renders implausible numbers or undefined properties, check these OpenWeatherMap schema behaviors: Observed symptom Root cause Resolution Temperature reads 280–310 Omitting units returns Kelvin (K) under the default standard unit system. Append &units=metric (°C) or &units=imperial (°F), or convert in UI code. See Unit systems and conversions. rain, snow, or wind.gust is undefined OpenWeatherMap omits optional precipitation and gust objects whenever accumulation is zero or unmeasured. Read optional fields defensively (data.rain?.['1h'] ?? 0 in JavaScript or data.get("rain", {}).get("1h", 0.0) in Python). main.temp_min equals main.temp_max In /data/2.5/weather, those fields reflect current spatial spread across stations in a metro area, not 24-hour daily lows and highs. Compute daily extremes across intervals in /data/2.5/forecast. See How weather data works. dt lags behind current time by up to 10 minutes dt records when the meteorological observation snapshot was calculated (refreshed every 10 minutes), not HTTP response time. Cache responses for 10 minutes instead of re-polling for newer timestamps. pressure is 1013 and rain.1h is in mm despite units=imperial units modifies only temperature and wind speed; pressure (hPa), precipitation (mm), and visibility (m) always remain in SI units. Convert mm ÷ 25.4 for inches and hPa × 0.02953 for inHg. See Unit systems and conversions. Strict data.cod === 200 check fails cod is serialized as a number (200) in /data/2.5/weather and as a string ("200") in /data/2.5/forecast. Branch on the HTTP transport status (response.ok or response.status) instead of data.cod.

OpenWeatherMap's default Free plan gives you 60 calls per minute and 1,000,000 calls per month across Weather API 2.5 (/data/2.5/weather and /data/2.5/forecast) and Geocoding API 1.0 (/geo/1.0/direct, /geo/1.0/reverse, and /geo/1.0/zip) with no credit card required. documents.t: Weather API 2.5 and Geocoding API 1.0 are included automatically on every free OpenWeatherMap account without entering billing information. One Call API 3.0 (/data/3.0/onecall) is a separate "One Call by Call" pay-as-you-go product that bundles current, minute-by-minute, hourly, and 8-day daily forecasts into one endpoint. Even though One Call API 3.0 includes 1,000 free calls per day, activating /data/3.0/onecall requires adding a payment method (and setting a daily call cap if you want to prevent overage charges). Calling /data/3.0/onecall with a standard free-tier key without an active One Call subscription returns 401 Unauthorized. Everything documented on this site uses the free-tier 2.5 and 1.0 endpoints.

documents.t: Newly generated API keys take 10–15 minutes on average—and up to 2 hours during peak synchronization windows—to propagate across OpenWeatherMap's global edge servers. Wait at least 15 minutes and test against /data/2.5/weather before generating another key. If 401 persists past 2 hours, verify that your key is marked Active in your dashboard and that your URL uses /data/2.5/weather rather than /data/3.0/onecall. See Common errors for a curl diagnostic check.
documents.s: Why does my newly created API key return a 401 Unauthorized error?

documents.t: No. OpenWeatherMap enforces the 60 calls per minute and 1,000,000 calls per month quotas across your entire account, pooling traffic from every active key you generate. Creating separate keys is useful for isolating credentials between development, staging, and production environments so you can rotate one key without disrupting others—not for expanding throughput. To scale to thousands of users within the free quota, see Set up rate limiting and caching.
documents.s: Do multiple API keys under one account increase my rate limit?

documents.t: When you omit the units query parameter, OpenWeatherMap defaults to the standard unit system and returns temperatures in Kelvin (K). Append &units=metric for Celsius (°C) or &units=imperial for Fahrenheit (°F). Remember that units affects only temperature and wind speed: pressure (hPa), precipitation (mm), and visibility (m) remain in SI units across all three modes. See Unit systems and conversions for the complete field matrix and conversion formulas.
documents.s: Why does the API return temperatures around 285 to 305?

documents.t: In /data/2.5/weather, main.temp_min and main.temp_max do not represent the 24-hour daily low and high forecast. Instead, they report instantaneous spatial temperature variation across reporting stations within a large metropolitan region. In smaller cities or single-grid-cell locations, temp, temp_min, and temp_max hold the exact same value. To calculate upcoming daily highs and lows on the free tier, aggregate intervals from /data/2.5/forecast. See How weather data works for details.
documents.s: Why does temp_min equal temp_max in current weather responses?

documents.t: OpenWeatherMap omits optional precipitation (rain, snow) and wind gust (wind.gust) properties whenever no measurable accumulation or gust was observed during that interval, rather than returning 0. Always read optional properties defensively—such as data.rain?.['1h'] ?? 0 in JavaScript or data.get("rain", {}).get("1h", 0.0) in Python. For the full schema, see Current weather reference.
documents.s: Why do rain, snow, or wind.gust fields disappear from some responses?

documents.t: City names frequently collide across countries and states (for example, dozens of municipalities share the name "Springfield" or "San Jose"), and non-ASCII characters require URL encoding. Instead of passing city strings directly to /data/2.5/weather?q=, resolve the place name through the Geocoding API (/geo/1.0/direct) first and pass the resulting lat and lon coordinates to the weather endpoint. Follow the step-by-step recipe in Query weather by coordinates.
documents.s: Why did my city name search return 404 or resolve to the wrong country?

documents.t: During local prototyping, a preflight-exempt GET request from browser JavaScript to https://api.openweathermap.org succeeds as long as your HTTP client doesn't attach custom headers such as Authorization or Content-Type: application/json (which trigger OPTIONS preflight checks that OpenWeatherMap blocks under CORS). For any public or multi-user production application, however, do not call OpenWeatherMap directly from a React or Vue frontend: Exposed credentials: Every visitor can read your appid in browser DevTools network logs and reuse your quota. Uncoalesced rate limits: Concurrent visitors multiply upstream traffic linearly and trip 429 Too Many Requests once traffic exceeds 60 requests per minute. Route frontend requests through a lightweight backend proxy (such as an Express route, FastAPI endpoint, Next.js Route Handler, or serverless worker) that stores OPENWEATHER_API_KEY on the server and caches responses for 10 minutes. See API architecture overview and Common errors.
documents.s: Can I call OpenWeatherMap directly from a React or Vue frontend?

documents.t: Yes. OpenWeatherMap licenses free-tier data under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International license (CC BY-SA 4.0), which permits both personal and commercial applications as long as you satisfy its license obligations—specifically crediting OpenWeatherMap as the source (for example, displaying "Weather data provided by OpenWeatherMap" linked to OpenWeatherMap) and applying compatible share-alike terms if you redistribute adapted datasets. Paid enterprise tiers provide commercial licensing options with adjusted attribution terms; review the official OpenWeatherMap pricing and terms before launching a commercial product.

documents.t: If you encounter an issue that isn't resolved by Common errors or the FAQ, gather a clean diagnostic snapshot before searching community trackers or opening an upstream support ticket.

Redact your API key before sharing logs Never paste a live appid value into GitHub issues, Stack Overflow questions, forum threads, or screenshots. Replace your credential with appid=REDACTED in every URL and log snippet before publishing. If you accidentally expose a live key in public, revoke it immediately in the OpenWeatherMap API keys dashboard and generate a replacement. Collect these four diagnostic details before posting a question or filing a bug report: Isolate SDK and browser layers with a minimal curl request: Run the failing query directly from a terminal using curl -i against https://api.openweathermap.org. If curl returns 200 OK while your application fails, the bug lies in your HTTP client configuration, environment variable loading, third-party SDK wrapper, or browser CORS headers rather than OpenWeatherMap's servers: curl -i "https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?lat=51.5074&lon=-0.1278&units=metric&appid=REDACTED" Record the exact endpoint URL and query parameters: Include the full versioned path (/data/2.5/weather, /data/2.5/forecast, or /geo/1.0/direct) and every query parameter (lat, lon, q, zip, units, lang) with appid=REDACTED. Capture the HTTP transport status and raw response body: Copy both the HTTP status line (for example, HTTP/2 401 or HTTP/2 429) and the exact JSON payload (or gateway HTML error text) returned by the server. Note the UTC timestamp of the failed call: Record when the failure occurred in ISO 8601 UTC format (such as 2026-11-18T14:25:00Z) so support engineers can correlate edge gateway logs and per-minute quota windows.

This portfolio documentation covers the free-tier Weather API 2.5 and Geocoding API 1.0 surface. For paid plans, historical archives, weather maps, and upstream policy updates, consult OpenWeatherMap's official documentation: Official OpenWeatherMap API documentation for the complete catalog of free, pay-as-you-go, and enterprise weather APIs OpenWeatherMap pricing and plan comparison for endpoint availability, call quotas, and commercial licensing terms across tiers OpenWeatherMap official FAQ for account management, billing administration, and subscription troubleshooting

When a minimal curl command succeeds in your terminal, the root cause almost always involves language-specific HTTP handling (such as JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, or Go), UI framework lifecycle hooks (such as React, Vue, or Next.js), or a community wrapper library: Search Stack Overflow questions tagged openweathermap for solutions to framework integration patterns, async state bugs, and coordinate formatting issues. If you use a third-party client wrapper (such as pyowm for Python or community TypeScript SDKs), search the Issues tab of that library's GitHub repository to check whether the wrapper targets deprecated endpoint paths or requires a configuration flag for Weather API 2.5.

documents.t: If you reproduce a persistent 5xx upstream error with curl, experience 401 Unauthorized on /data/2.5/weather more than 2 hours after activating a key, or need assistance with account billing and enterprise quotas, contact the vendor's support team directly through the OpenWeatherMap support center. Include your redacted URL, HTTP status code, raw response body, and UTC timestamp in your ticket. In this tutorial, you'll build a Python command-line interface (weather.py) that accepts any city name and unit system flag (metric, imperial, or standard) and prints live weather conditions in your terminal. Time: 20–25 minutes Level: Intermediate What you'll build: A standalone Python CLI application (weather.py) inside a virtual environment that parses command-line flags, fetches live OpenWeatherMap data, formats unit-accurate output, and exits cleanly with actionable error messages. What you'll learn: Isolate project dependencies inside a .venv virtual environment. Parse multi-word city names and optional --units flags with argparse. Map temperature (°C, °F, K) and wind speed (m/s, mph) units accurately across OpenWeatherMap unit modes. Handle HTTP status codes, network timeouts, and optional JSON fields safely using requests, sys.stderr, and sys.exit(1).
documents.s: Build a weather CLI tool in Python

documents.t: Environment and credentials: Completed the Getting started guide, with OPENWEATHER_API_KEY set in your active terminal session. Runtime: Python 3.10 or later installed. Code editor: Visual Studio Code or another text editor.

Create a weather-cli project directory, initialize and activate a .venv virtual environment, install requests, and create an empty weather.py script. macOS / Linux Windows (PowerShell) mkdir weather-cli && cd weather-cli python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install requests touch weather.py New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path weather-cli | Out-Null Set-Location weather-cli python -m venv .venv; .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 python -m pip install requests New-Item -ItemType File -Path weather.py | Out-Null If PowerShell blocks .ps1 activation scripts, run Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass for the current window and run .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 again. When activation succeeds, your shell prompt displays (.venv) at the beginning of the line, and python points to the virtual environment interpreter on all operating systems.
documents.s: Step 1: Create a virtual environment and install dependencies

documents.t: Open weather.py in Visual Studio Code and define your imports, API endpoint constant, and temperature unit lookup dictionary. weather.py import argparse import os import sys import requests BASE_URL = "https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather" TEMP_UNITS = { "metric": "°C", "imperial": "°F", "standard": "K", }
documents.s: Step 2: Add imports, constants, and unit mappings

documents.t: Append build_parser to weather.py. Using nargs="+" on city lets callers pass multi-word city names such as New York or Rio de Janeiro with or without surrounding quotation marks. weather.py def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser( description="Fetch current weather conditions for a city from OpenWeatherMap." ) parser.add_argument( "city", nargs="+", help="City name, such as London or New York (quotes optional).", ) parser.add_argument( "-u", "--units", choices=["metric", "imperial", "standard"], default="metric", help="Unit system for temperature and wind speed (default: metric).", ) return parser

Test your argument parser before writing the network layer. Temporarily append these two lines to the bottom of weather.py. weather.py if __name__ == "__main__": build_parser().parse_args() Run weather.py with the --help flag. python weather.py --help Expected output: usage: weather.py [-h] [-u {metric,imperial,standard}] city [city ...] Fetch current weather conditions for a city from OpenWeatherMap. positional arguments: city City name, such as London or New York (quotes optional). options: -h, --help show this help message and exit -u, --units {metric,imperial,standard} Unit system for temperature and wind speed (default: metric). Remove the temporary two-line if __name__ == "__main__": block before continuing to Step 4.

documents.t: Append get_weather and main to weather.py. OpenWeatherMap returns wind speed in m/s for both standard and metric modes and switches to mph only when units is imperial, so wind_unit checks specifically for "imperial". All failure paths write to sys.stderr and exit with status code 1. weather.py def get_weather(city: str, units: str, api_key: str) -> None: params = { "q": city, "appid": api_key, "units": units, } try: response = requests.get(BASE_URL, params=params, timeout=10) response.raise_for_status() data = response.json() except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as http_err: status_code = ( http_err.response.status_code if http_err.response is not None else None ) if status_code == 404: print(f"Error: City '{city}' was not found.", file=sys.stderr) elif status_code == 401: print( "Error: Authentication failed (HTTP 401). Check your OPENWEATHER_API_KEY value and activation status.", file=sys.stderr, ) elif status_code == 429: print( "Error: Rate limit exceeded (HTTP 429). Wait a minute before retrying.", file=sys.stderr, ) else: print(f"HTTP error: {http_err}", file=sys.stderr) sys.exit(1) except requests.exceptions.Timeout: print( "Error: Request timed out after 10 seconds. Check your network connection.", file=sys.stderr, ) sys.exit(1) except requests.exceptions.RequestException as req_err: print(f"Network error: {req_err}", file=sys.stderr) sys.exit(1) name = data.get("name", city) country = data.get("sys", {}).get("country", "") location = f"{name}, {country}" if country else name weather_entries = data.get("weather") or [{}] condition = weather_entries[0].get("description", "unavailable").capitalize() main_readings = data.get("main", {}) temp = main_readings.get("temp", 0.0) feels_like = main_readings.get("feels_like", 0.0) humidity = main_readings.get("humidity", 0) wind_speed = data.get("wind", {}).get("speed", 0.0) temp_unit = TEMP_UNITS[units] wind_unit = "mph" if units == "imperial" else "m/s" print(f"Weather in {location}") print(f" Condition: {condition}") print(f" Temperature: {temp:.1f}{temp_unit} (feels like {feels_like:.1f}{temp_unit})") print(f" Humidity: {humidity}%") print(f" Wind speed: {wind_speed:.1f} {wind_unit}") def main() -> None: parser = build_parser() args = parser.parse_args() api_key = os.environ.get("OPENWEATHER_API_KEY") if not api_key: print( "Error: Missing OPENWEATHER_API_KEY environment variable. Set it before running weather.py.", file=sys.stderr, ) sys.exit(1) city_name = " ".join(args.city) get_weather(city_name, args.units, api_key) if __name__ == "__main__": main() Expand the block below to verify your file against the complete script before running it. In this tutorial, you'll build a command-line weather dashboard in Node.js that fetches live conditions for five cities concurrently and renders an aligned summary table in your terminal. Time: 15–20 minutes Level: Beginner What you'll build: An ES module script (dashboard.mjs) that queries the OpenWeatherMap API in parallel, isolates single-city failures, and prints a formatted multi-city weather table. What you'll learn: Validate environment credentials upfront before sending network requests. Construct safe query strings with URL and URLSearchParams and enforce timeouts with AbortSignal.timeout. Fetch multiple cities concurrently with Promise.all without letting one failed request crash the batch. Align negative, single-digit, and double-digit readings into fixed-width terminal columns.

documents.t: Environment and credentials: Completed the Getting started guide, with OPENWEATHER_API_KEY set in your active terminal session. Runtime: Node.js 20 LTS or later installed (Node.js 18 and later include native fetch and AbortSignal.timeout). Code editor: Visual Studio Code or another text editor.

Create a weather-dashboard directory, navigate into it, and create an empty dashboard.mjs file. Using the .mjs extension tells Node.js to load the file as an ECMAScript module with top-level await support. macOS / Linux Windows (PowerShell) mkdir weather-dashboard && cd weather-dashboard touch dashboard.mjs New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path weather-dashboard | Out-Null Set-Location weather-dashboard New-Item -ItemType File -Path dashboard.mjs | Out-Null

documents.t: Open dashboard.mjs in Visual Studio Code and add the API key guard, endpoint URL constant, and list of cities to monitor. Checking process.env.OPENWEATHER_API_KEY at startup fails fast with a clear message instead of sending five unauthenticated 401 requests. dashboard.mjs const API_KEY = process.env.OPENWEATHER_API_KEY; const BASE_URL = "https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather"; if (!API_KEY) { console.error( "Error: Missing OPENWEATHER_API_KEY environment variable. Set it before running dashboard.mjs." ); process.exit(1); } const cities = ["London", "New York", "Tokyo", "Rio de Janeiro", "Sydney"];

documents.t: Append the getWeather function to dashboard.mjs. It encodes query parameters with URLSearchParams, enforces a 10-second timeout with AbortSignal.timeout(10000), extracts OpenWeatherMap's message field when !response.ok, and returns null on failure so a single bad request doesn't abort other cities. dashboard.mjs async function getWeather(city) { const url = new URL(BASE_URL); url.search = new URLSearchParams({ q: city, units: "metric", appid: API_KEY, }).toString(); try { const response = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10000), }); if (!response.ok) { const errorBody = await response.json().catch(() => null); const detail = errorBody?.message ?? response.statusText; throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status} (${detail})`); } return await response.json(); } catch (error) { console.error(`Warning: Failed to fetch "${city}" - ${error.message}`); return null; } }

documents.t: Confirm that your credentials and getWeather function work before building the table formatter. Temporarily append these four lines to the bottom of dashboard.mjs. dashboard.mjs const sample = await getWeather("London"); if (sample) { console.log(`Verified: ${sample.name} (${sample.main.temp.toFixed(1)}°C)`); } Run dashboard.mjs from your terminal. node dashboard.mjs Expected output: Verified: London (12.3°C) Live temperature values vary with current weather conditions in London. Remove the temporary sample lines from the bottom of dashboard.mjs before moving to Step 4.

Append the formatWeather helper to dashboard.mjs. Right-padding text columns (padEnd) and left-padding numeric columns (padStart—including `${main.temp.toFixed(1)}°C`.padStart(8)) keeps negative, single-digit, and double-digit values aligned across every row. dashboard.mjs function formatWeather(data) { if (!data) { return null; } const { name, sys, main, weather, wind } = data; const location = (sys?.country ? `${name}, ${sys.country}` : name).padEnd(20); const temp = `${main.temp.toFixed(1)}°C`.padStart(8); const condition = (weather?.[0]?.description ?? "unavailable").padEnd(24); const humidity = `${main.humidity}%`.padStart(8); const windSpeed = `${wind.speed.toFixed(1)} m/s`.padStart(10); return ` ${location} ${temp} ${condition} ${humidity} ${windSpeed}`; }

Append runDashboard and invoke it at the bottom of dashboard.mjs. Calling Promise.all(cities.map(getWeather)) dispatches all five HTTP requests concurrently rather than waiting for each city sequentially. dashboard.mjs async function runDashboard() { const divider = "=".repeat(80); const header = [ ` ${"City".padEnd(20)}`, "Temp".padStart(8), "Condition".padEnd(24), "Humidity".padStart(8), "Wind".padStart(10), ].join(" "); const subdivider = [ ` ${"-".repeat(20)}`, "-".repeat(8), "-".repeat(24), "-".repeat(8), "-".repeat(10), ].join(" "); const results = await Promise.all(cities.map(getWeather)); const rows = results.map(formatWeather).filter(Boolean); console.log(divider); console.log(" Current weather dashboard"); console.log(divider); console.log(header); console.log(subdivider); for (const row of rows) { console.log(row); } console.log(divider); console.log( ` Last updated: ${new Date().toISOString()} (${rows.length}/${cities.length} cities)` ); } await runDashboard(); Expand the block below to compare your file against the complete script before running it.
